title: TWO "WANT-TO-GO-HOME" HEADACHE CURES
text:
THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE 103

NO WANT-TO-GO-HOME HEADACHE CURES—Mrs. E. A. McMahon remembers that disciplinary touches of the gentler and more nurturing variety began with the earliest school days.

Mattie Patton (Mattie Patton) and I first started to school, and we had a game that we played on Mr. Dick Gay, our teacher, each day to get to go home early; that is, each day (by the time it was often embarrassing, but we made the best of it by the time it was often embarrassing, but we made the best of it—we had become such good friends) that we would tell Mr. Dick Gay, our teacher, each day that we had a headache and wanted to go home. For a month we did this, and the teacher, of course, was very soon disgusted with our game of truancy every day that they played truant daily together. After that Mattie gave Mattie a little whipping one morning before we left for school, and after that each morning before we left with me, and of course we had no more headaches.

Miss Ella Scott was at our house and I think Mattie Scott must have known about it too. When Mattie's mother came home, we told her "Mattie is sick." So she came in and was very sorry for us too. They all sat in the sitting room until nearly supper time. When we really got pot[?], until we really got pot[?], and had our supper without him, returned to their seats, and without batting an eye, sat down and had our supper until finally nearly supper time.

†Personal items from Mrs. E. A. McMahon (Gala Chenault), Dallas, Texas, June 20, 1938.
notes: Page 103 of printed book. Some passages difficult to read due to scan quality; one word transcribed as pot[?]. Footnote cites personal items from Mrs. E. A. McMahon (Gala Chenault).
